The server now utilizes `express.json()` middleware to parse incoming JSON payloads, which is required for the `/login` endpoint to access `req.body` (ev_2).

concepts.name: Router

concepts.name: Middleware
concepts.explanation: Functions that run during the request-response cycle. `express.json()` is middleware that converts the raw request body into a JavaScript object (ev_2).

concepts.name: Asynchronous functions
concepts.explanation: The use of `async` and `await` allows the server to wait for the `verifyPassword` check to complete without blocking other requests (ev_1).

tasks.title: Initialize project and setup Express server
acceptanceCriteria: Server starts on a defined port
A GET /health endpoint returns a 200 OK status
Project contains a package.json with express dependency

tasks.title: Implement User Authentication (Login)
acceptanceCriteria: POST /login endpoint accepts username and password
Successful login returns a JWT or session token
Invalid credentials return a 401 Unauthorized status

tasks.title: Create Todo CRUD endpoints
acceptanceCriteria: POST /todos creates a new todo item
GET /todos returns a list of todos for the authenticated user
PUT /todos/:id updates an existing todo item

tasks.title: Implement Authentication Middleware
acceptanceCriteria: Protected endpoints return 401 Unauthorized if no token is provided
Protected endpoints return 403 Forbidden if the token is invalid

tasks.title: Integrate Data Persistence
acceptanceCriteria: Todo items persist across server restarts
User credentials are stored securely (e.g., hashed passwords)
